title: Cambricon-D: Full-Network Differential Acceleration for Diffusion Models
problem: Diffusion models require repetitive full model recalculations across timesteps on minimally altered input data, creating computational redundancy. Non-linear operations necessitate repeatedly merging deltas with raw inputs, causing substantial memory access bottlenecks that block delta forwarding throughout the network.
motivation: Diffusion models are prominent in image generation but current approaches incur remarkable computational redundancy and substantial hardware expenditures.
method: Cambricon-D employs a sign-mask dataflow that loads only 1-bit signs instead of full bitwidth raw inputs, enabling seamless delta forwarding through the network. This approach maintains differential computing efficiency while reducing memory access overhead for non-linear operations by requiring only sign information to merge deltas with raw inputs for activation functions.
key_novelty: Sign-mask dataflow that enables full-network differential computing with minimal memory access by loading only 1-bit signs instead of complete raw input data.
contributions: Proposes Cambricon-D architecture with sign-mask dataflow for full-network differential acceleration
Reduces off-chip memory access by 66-82% compared to Diffy baseline
Achieves 1.46x-2.38x speedup over A100 GPU on various diffusion models
Maintains computational correctness for non-linear operations while enabling seamless delta forwarding
